info.title: OpenPartner API
info.description:
The OpenPartner tenant API: partners, programs, links, attribution, commissions, payouts, reporting, webhooks and export. Use it to run a referral or affiliate program from your own backend, for example an in-app "Refer & earn" page with no separate OpenPartner login. Walkthrough: [Build an in-app referral page](https://github.com/getcoherence/openpartner/blob/main/docs/headless-referral.md). This document is generated from the API's own request validators. It is served at `/openapi.json`, and the rendered reference at `/docs`, on every deployment. White-label custom domains don't serve them; use the platform host, e.g. `https://app.openpartner.dev/api/docs`. ## Base URL and tenancy Every path below is relative to your tenant's API base: | Deployment | API base | Share links | | --- | --- | --- | | OpenPartner Cloud | `https://app.openpartner.dev/api/t/` | `https://app.openpartner.dev/r//` | | Cloud with a white-label domain | `https:///api` | `https:///r/` | | Self-hosted, single tenant | your API origin, e.g. `https://api.example.com` (or `/api` behind the bundled proxy) | `/r/` | | Self-hosted, multi-tenant | `/t/` (or `/api/t/`) | `/r//` | The slug comes **after** `/api`. `https://app.openpartner.dev/t//api/...` reaches the portal's static site, not the API, and returns HTML. On a multi-tenant deployment a request with no `/t/` prefix fails with `400 tenant_slug_missing`, and an unknown slug gets a plain `404`. Your slug is the `/t//` segment in your admin portal's address. **Publisher sub-IDs.** A partner may add `?sub_id=` to a share link (trimmed, at most 255 characters). The router stores it on the click and doesn't pass it to your destination. It comes back as `subId` on `commission.*` webhooks and in the partner's `{sub_id}` postback macro, so a publisher's tracking tool can match each conversion to its own click. Keys minted through the API are bound to their tenant. A key sent to another tenant's path is `401 unauthorized`. ## Authentication Send a key as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer op_…`. Keys are server-side credentials: never ship one to a browser or mobile app. There are three kinds: - **Admin key.** Unscoped, full access to the tenant. Minted with `POST /api-keys`, or the deployment's `ADMIN_API_KEY` (self-host). The admin portal's session cookie is accepted wherever an admin key is. - **Scoped key.** Minted with `POST /api-keys/scoped` and a list of scopes. It can call only the operations its scopes unlock, and it acts on any partner in the tenant. Calling something it lacks the scope for returns `403 forbidden_scope` with the `required` scope; calling an operation with no scope returns `403 forbidden`. Use one for every integration so a leaked key can't do everything. - **Partner key.** Minted with `POST /partners/{id}/api-keys` by an admin or the partner. It acts as that one partner and can only reach that partner's own resources (`/partners/{its id}/…`). Revoking the partner revokes its keys. Each operation says which of these it accepts. Scopes: | Scope | Unlocks | | --- | --- | | `bonuses:write` | `POST /bonuses`
`GET /bonuses`
`GET /bonuses/{id}` | | `clicks:write` | `POST /clicks` | | `commissions:read` | `GET /partners/{id}/commissions`
`GET /commissions`
`GET /bonuses`
`GET /bonuses/{id}` | | `events:write` | `POST /attribution/events`
`POST /attribution/conversions`
`POST /attribution/refunds`
`POST /coupons/redeem` | | `links:read` | `GET /partners/{id}/links` | | `links:write` | `POST /partners/{id}/links` | | `partners:create` | `POST /partners` | | `partners:read` | `GET /partners`
`GET /partners/{id}`
`GET /partners/{id}/dashboard`
`GET /partners/{id}/timeseries`
`GET /partners/{id}/events`
`GET /partners/{id}/customers`
`GET /partners/{id}/breakdowns`
`GET /partners/{id}/referrals` | | `partners:signin` | `POST /partners/{id}/signin-link`
`POST /partners/signin-link` | | `partners:write` | `POST /partners`
`PATCH /partners/{id}`
`POST /import/partners-csv`
`POST /partners/{id}/invite`
`POST /partners/{id}/revoke`
`POST /partners/{id}/coupons`
`DELETE /partners/{id}/coupons/{couponId}` | | `payout_profiles:read` | `GET /partners/{id}/payout-profile` | | `payout_profiles:write` | `GET /partners/{id}/payout-profile`
`PUT /partners/{id}/payout-profile`
`DELETE /partners/{id}/payout-profile` | | `payouts:read` | `GET /payouts`
`GET /partners/{id}/payouts`
`GET /payouts/{id}/statement` | | `webhooks:write` | `POST /webhooks`
`DELETE /webhooks/{id}` | `partners:read` also unlocks `GET /brand-resources` (brand logo, colours and shareable assets), which this reference doesn't cover yet. The OpenPartner Network federation key holds `partners:write`, `partners:read`, `links:write`, `commissions:read`, `clicks:write`, `bonuses:write`. **Scoped reads that don't exist yet:** `GET /partners/{id}/funnel`, `/coupons` and `/commission-snapshot` accept no scope. Read them with an admin key from your server, or use `/timeseries` (which has `partners:read`) for funnel-like counts. ## Requests and responses - JSON bodies (`content-type: application/json`), up to 1 MB. `POST /import` takes up to 256 MB on single-tenant installs. - Errors are `{ "error": "", "detail": … }`. Branch on `error`; `detail` is for humans. - **Timestamps are ISO-8601 in UTC and must end in `Z`**: `2026-10-16T10:00:00Z`. An offset such as `+00:00` (Python's `isoformat()` default) is rejected with `400 invalid_body` / `invalid_query`. - Money in major units. Commission and payout amounts, and `eventValue` in webhook payloads, are decimal **strings** such as `"12.50"`. Report endpoints (dashboard, timeseries, a partner's events list) return JSON numbers. - Fields may be added to any response at any time. Ignore fields you don't know. - Send `X-Request-Id` to correlate a call; every response echoes one back (generated if you didn't send it). Quote it in support requests. ## Idempotency `POST /attribution/events`, `POST /attribution/conversions`, `POST /attribution/refunds` and `POST /coupons/redeem` take an `externalEventId`: your stable id for that one event (required on conversions and refunds). A retry with the same key replays the original result (`replayed: true`) and records nothing, even when the duplicates arrive at the same moment. A key reused for a different event is `409 external_event_id_conflict`. `POST /clicks` is idempotent on the click `id`, and `POST /bonuses` on its optional `externalRef` (reused for a different partner, program, amount or currency: `409 external_ref_conflict`). Other writes are not idempotent: `POST /partners` answers a duplicate email with `409 email_taken`, so look the partner up with `GET /partners?email=`. ## Pagination `GET /partners`, the commission lists and `GET /payouts` are keyset-paginated: pass the response's `nextCursor` as `cursor` until it is `null`. Cursors are opaque. `GET /partners/{id}/events` and `/customers` use `limit` + `offset`. `GET /partners/{id}/payouts` returns the 200 most recent, and `GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries` the 100 most recent. ## Rate limits The API shares one limit of **600 requests per 5 minutes per client IP** across its routes (a few infrastructure paths are exempt). A backend calls from one IP, so that is your whole integration's budget, event ingest included: at four calls per page view, about 150 uncached page views per 5 minutes. Cache partner stats for a few minutes, don't let users force a refresh, and report events from a queue that backs off on `429`. Over the limit you get `429 rate_limited` with the IETF `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers. `POST /attribution/identify` has its own limit of 120 per minute per IP, answered with `429 rate_limited` and `Retry-After`. When the browser SDK calls it, that is each visitor's IP; when your backend calls it, every stitch counts against your backend's IP, so prefer the browser for identify at volume. ## Webhooks Subscribe with `POST /webhooks`; the event catalogue is under **Webhook events**. Each delivery is a JSON `POST` of an envelope `{ id, event, created, data }` with: | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `X-OpenPartner-Signature` | hex HMAC-SHA256 of `.`, keyed with the endpoint's secret (the whole `whsec_…` string) | | `X-OpenPartner-Timestamp` | Unix seconds when the attempt was signed | | `X-OpenPartner-Event` | the event type | | `X-OpenPartner-Delivery` | the envelope `id` | To verify a delivery, recompute the HMAC over the **raw** request body, before any JSON parsing, and compare it in constant time. Reject timestamps more than 5 minutes from now. Then dedupe on `id`: ```js import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto'; function verify(rawBody, headers, secret) { const ts = headers['x-openpartner-timestamp']; const sig = headers['x-openpartner-signature'] ?? ''; if (!ts || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(ts)) > 300) return false; const expected = Buffer.from(createHmac('sha256', secret).update(`${ts}.${rawBody}`).digest('hex')); const given = Buffer.from(sig); return given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(given, expected); } ``` Delivery is at most once per trigger: a non-2xx answer, a redirect, or no answer within 10 seconds marks the delivery failed, and **failed deliveries are not retried automatically**. Find them with `GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries` and resend with `POST /webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{deliveryId}/retry`. A resend carries the same `id` and a fresh signature. Treat webhooks as notifications and the list endpoints as the record: reconcile from `GET /commissions` if you can't afford to miss one. Endpoints must be publicly reachable. Private, loopback and link-local destinations are refused at delivery time, and OpenPartner Cloud delivers only to ports 80 and 443. A single-tenant self-host can allow specific private ranges with `OPENPARTNER_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS`.

adminKey.description: An unscoped admin key (`POST /api-keys`), or the deployment's `ADMIN_API_KEY`. Full access to the tenant it was minted in. Server-side only.

scopedKey.description: A scoped key (`POST /api-keys/scoped`). Each operation lists the one scope that unlocks it; a key without it gets `403 forbidden_scope`. Operations that list no scope reject scoped keys.

partnerKey.description: A partner-scoped key (`POST /partners/{id}/api-keys`). Acts as that one partner: it can read and write only that partner's own resources.

postbackToken.name: token
postbackToken.description: The conversion postback token (`opcp_…`), minted and rotated under Admin → Integrations. It travels in the URL, so proxies, browser history and the sender's own logs keep it. It is built to be cheap to leak: it records conversions and nothing else, is never accepted as a Bearer key, can be pinned to the sender's IPs, and rotating it kills the old URL at once. Only `GET /postback` takes it.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON you supplied at creation. OpenPartner may add a `network` key when the partner is synced to the Network.

activatedAt.description: Null until the partner accepts their invite. `sendInvite: false` sets it at creation.

portalAccess.description: May the partner sign in to the partner portal? `false`: `POST /auth/signin` sends them nothing (answering as it does for an unknown email), password and Google sign-in turn them away the same way, their sessions end, and no invite or portal email goes to them. For headless programs. Set it on `POST /partners` or `PATCH /partners/{id}`.

detail.description: Human-readable cause, or zod `flatten()` output for `invalid_body` / `invalid_query`.

Error.description: Every non-2xx response. `error` is stable and safe to branch on; `detail` is for humans and may change. Some errors carry extra fields (e.g. `required` on `forbidden_scope`, `matureAt` on `holdback_active`).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

url.description: Redirect the partner's browser here. It signs them in to the partner portal, once, and lands on `returnTo` (or their dashboard). On your white-label domain when one is verified.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after minting. Unused by then, the link fails.

programId.description: Null for partner-wide terms; set for terms on that one program.

recurring.description: Keeps paying on renewals, including renewals past the attribution window that the program's `renewalsStayWithPartner` carries. A rule without it pays only while the click that earned the customer is inside the window.

recurringMonths.description: Stop paying this many months after the customer's first attributed event of the rule's type for this partner. Omitted: no cap.

CommissionSnapshot.description: A per-partner commission override. When present it replaces the program's rule for this partner's future commissions: on every program (partner-wide, `programId` null) or on one program. On that program, program-scoped terms beat partner-wide ones.

Decimal.description: A decimal amount as a string, e.g. `"12.50"`. Major currency units.

CommissionBands.description: Value bands: the rate steps up with the event's value. The sub-rule's own `value` is the base band; `levels` lists the steps above it. `whole` pays the reached band's rate on the whole value, `marginal` pays each slice at its own band's rate.

CommissionTiers.description: Performance tiers: the rate steps up with the partner's own revenue or conversions over a window. Not combined with `bands`.

customerRewardDelivery.description: How customer-side rewards reach the customer on this deployment: minted in Stripe, not configured, or applied by the brand itself.

attributionWindowDays.description: How old a click may be and still win a customer's first conversion of an event type. With `renewalsStayWithPartner`, it doesn't limit renewals.

renewalsStayWithPartner.description: True (default): a repeat event, meaning a type the customer already has an attributed conversion of (the 2nd, 13th, 40th `invoice_paid`), keeps that first conversion's partners, weights and model whatever the click's age, and a later click from another partner doesn't take it. Past the window only `recurring` sub-rules pay on it, up to `recurringMonths`. False: every event is attributed on its own against the clicks inside the window.

holdbackDays.description: Above 0: commissions auto-approve this many days after accruing. 0 or null: they wait for a manual approve.

revenueEventTypes.description: Event types that are sales in this program beyond invoice_paid and subscription_created, which always are. Their value counts as partner-attributed revenue for the hosted platform fee.

recurring.description: Keeps paying on renewals, including renewals past the attribution window that the program's `renewalsStayWithPartner` carries. A rule without it pays only while the click that earned the customer is inside the window.

recurringMonths.description: Stop paying this many months after the customer's first attributed event of the rule's type for this partner. Omitted: no cap.

CommissionRule.description: An array of triggered sub-rules. Programs written through this API always store the array; rows created before compound rules may still hold the legacy single-rule object.

currency.description: The brand's default currency, for showing a zero. Amounts are in their own currencies.

partners.description: Partners enrolled in the program now, plus any with clicks, conversions or commission in it during the window.

attributedEvents.description: Conversions attributed in the window, counted per attribution: an event credited through two clicks (a multi-touch model) counts twice.

attributedRevenueByCurrency.description: Amount per ISO 4217 currency code. Currencies with nothing are absent; nothing is converted.

commissionByCurrency.description: Commission totals per currency, then per status. Currencies and statuses with nothing are absent.

programs.description: Every program, newest first, including programs with no activity.

source.description: Partner callers only: how the grant was made.

SaveWarnings.description: Present only when there is something to fix. Today: a Stripe Payment Link (`buy.stripe.com`, `checkout.stripe.com`) without `client_reference_id={click_id}`. Stripe reads the referral only from that parameter, so without it no purchase through the link can be credited to the partner.

commission.description: This partner's terms on this program (setPartnerProgramCommission). Null: the partner-wide override, or the program's own rule, applies.

destinationUrl.description: Deep-link override. Null = the program's destinationUrl.

Link.description: A partner share link. The public URL is built from the router base, not stored: `https://app.openpartner.dev/r/<tenantSlug>/<linkKey>` on OpenPartner Cloud, `https://<custom-domain>/r/<linkKey>` on a white-label domain, `<router-origin>/r/<linkKey>` self-hosted.

LinkSaved.description: A partner share link. The public URL is built from the router base, not stored: `https://app.openpartner.dev/r/<tenantSlug>/<linkKey>` on OpenPartner Cloud, `https://<custom-domain>/r/<linkKey>` on a white-label domain, `<router-origin>/r/<linkKey>` self-hosted.

firstStitch.description: False when this (cref, userId) pair was already stitched; nothing was written.

backfilledAttributions.description: Events already recorded for this userId that attributed now that the click is known.

replayed.description: Present when an earlier call with the same `externalEventId` already recorded this event. `eventId` and `attribution` are that call's.

status.description: `outside_window`: no click is inside the window and the customer has no earlier attributed conversion to carry it (or the program has `renewalsStayWithPartner` off). A renewal of an attributed conversion attributes whatever the click's age. `not_attributed` appears only on a replay of an event that did not attribute the first time; which miss it was is not stored. `corrective`: a `refund`, `chargeback`, `dispute_created` or `invoice_payment_failed` event, recorded but never attributed. It reverses nothing; report refunds to `POST /attribution/refunds`.

commission.description: Present when `status` is `attributed`. `accrued`: at least one commission was written. `no_matching_rule`: no commission rule on the partner's terms takes this event type, so nothing is paid. Usually a typo'd stage name (`funded` for `loan_funded`); such types are listed under `GET /attribution/unmatched-event-types`. `none`: a rule takes the type but nothing accrued (the program has ended, a `first` rule already paid, a cap was reached, or the amount came to zero). On a replay with no commission, checked against the rules as they are now.

externalEventId.description: Idempotency key: your stable id for this one event, up to 120 characters. A number is used as its string. `null`, `""` or a blank string mean no key.

userId.description: The user the click was stitched to: your `userId`, or the click's own synthetic user when you sent none.

outcome.description: What the conversion came to. `attributed`: a partner was credited (check `reason` and `attribution.commission`). `no_matching_rule`: a partner was credited, but no commission rule takes this `type`, so nothing is paid: check the stage name. `not_attributed`: no partner was credited (see `reason`). The conversion is recorded either way, so don't retry it. `GET /postback` answers the same words as text.

reason.description: With `attributed`: `no_commission` when a rule takes the type but nothing accrued. With `not_attributed`: `outside_window` (the click is older than the program's attribution window, or newer than the conversion's `ts`), `no_click` (the partner was revoked), `corrective` (a `refund`, `chargeback`, `dispute_created` or `invoice_payment_failed` type, which is recorded but never attributed; report refunds to `POST /attribution/refunds`). A replay of a miss carries no reason, because which miss it was isn't stored.

replayed.description: Present when an earlier call with the same `externalEventId` already recorded this conversion. `eventId` and `attribution` are that call's.

externalEventId.description: Idempotency key: your stable id for this one conversion (a loan or transaction id), up to 120 characters. A number is used as its string.

prefix.description: The start of the token, `opcp_…`, to tell tokens apart. The full token is shown only once.

ipAllowlist.description: IP addresses or CIDR ranges `GET /postback` accepts calls from. Empty: any address.

events.description: Attributed events of this type since `since` that no rule took.

refundEventId.description: The corrective event recorded for this refund.

amount.description: This refund's amount, positive. Null for a refund of a conversion with no value.

refundedAmount.description: Everything refunded on this conversion so far, this refund included. Null when the conversion has no value.

fullRefund.description: Nothing of the conversion is left.

actionRequired.description: Some commission is `held_in_transfer` (retry later) or `clawback_recorded` (the partner was already paid; usually deducted from their next payout, see `clawback_recorded`).

commissions.description: One entry per commission the conversion accrued; empty when no partner was credited.

replayed.description: Present when an earlier call with the same `externalEventId` recorded this refund. Nothing new is recorded; the refund is re-applied, which finishes any commission that was held in transfer, and `commissions` shows where they stand now.

commissionId.description: The commission the conversion originally accrued.

allOf.description: What the partner keeps for this conversion now: the live commission's amount, or a paid one's amount net of adjustments.

status.description: `reversed`: unpaid, and nothing is kept (a full refund), so it was reversed. `reduced`: unpaid; reversed and replaced by `currentCommissionId` for the kept amount (a partial refund). `clawback_recorded`: already paid. It stays paid, and a negative adjustment of `clawbackAmount` records the refunded revenue the partner holds. OpenPartner deducts it from the partner's next manual or self-hosted Stripe Connect payout; funded Stripe Connect payouts on hosted OpenPartner don't, so recover those with the partner. `held_in_transfer`: a payout for it is in flight, so nothing changed. Retry this request (same `externalEventId`) once the payout settles. `unchanged`: nothing to take back.

currentCommissionId.description: The live commission row: the original, its replacement, or null once reversed.

clawbackAmount.description: Paid commissions only: the refund clawbacks recorded against it, negative. Null when none.

conversionExternalEventId.description: The `externalEventId` you sent with the conversion being refunded. Send this or `conversionEventId`, not both. A number is used as its string.

amount.description: Major units. Omit to refund everything not yet refunded.

externalEventId.description: Idempotency key: your stable id for this one refund (a refund or credit-note id), up to 120 characters. A number is used as its string.

brandChosen.description: The brand's admin typed this code. Only then does a Stripe promotion code or coupon the brand already had under the same string credit the partner.

canEdit.description: The program lets partners rename their own codes.

canEdit.description: The program lets partners rename their own codes.

attributionId.description: The attributed sale this commission was earned on. Null on a bonus's commission (`bonusId` is set instead).

bonusId.description: The bonus this commission pays (`POST /bonuses`). Null on a sale's commission.

status.description: `paid` means the commission is in a payout. On the manual rail that happens when the payout is planned, before the money is sent: check the payout's own `status`.

metadata.description: How the amount was worked out. `rateType` is the sub-rule's `percent` or `fixed` (absent on commissions accrued before October 2026). A banded or tiered rule also records `slab`: which sub-rule (`ruleIndex`), `kind` (`band` or `tier`), the `level` reached and its `threshold` and `value`, and for tiers the `metric` and its `metricValue` over the `window`. A replacement accrued for what a partial refund left records `refund`.

partnerName.description: The partner's name. Null only if the partner record is gone.

campaignName.description: The program's name (kept under its pre-rename key).

matureAt.description: When the holdback ends and the commission becomes approvable. Null = no holdback.

source.description: `attribution`: earned on an attributed sale. `bonus`: pays a bonus, with no event or click behind it.

eventType.description: The type of the attributed event the commission was earned on: `signup`, `trial_started`, `subscription_created`, `invoice_paid`, or one of your custom types. Null on a bonus's commission.

bountyName.description: The performance bounty's name, when a bounty paid it.

bonus.description: The bonus behind a `source: "bonus"` commission; null otherwise.

attributionId.description: The attributed sale this commission was earned on. Null on a bonus's commission (`bonusId` is set instead).

bonusId.description: The bonus this commission pays (`POST /bonuses`). Null on a sale's commission.

status.description: `paid` means the commission is in a payout. On the manual rail that happens when the payout is planned, before the money is sent: check the payout's own `status`.

metadata.description: How the amount was worked out. `rateType` is the sub-rule's `percent` or `fixed` (absent on commissions accrued before October 2026). A banded or tiered rule also records `slab`: which sub-rule (`ruleIndex`), `kind` (`band` or `tier`), the `level` reached and its `threshold` and `value`, and for tiers the `metric` and its `metricValue` over the `window`. A replacement accrued for what a partial refund left records `refund`.

replayed.description: Set on a replay of an `externalRef` already used: the original bonus.

source.description: `manual`: paid with `POST /bonuses` (an admin or your integration). `network`: an OpenPartner Network bounty, paid with the Network's federation key. `performance_bounty`: the partner reached a bounty's goal. New values may be added.

createdBy.description: The admin or API key that paid it; null for a performance bounty.

partnerName.description: The partner's name. Null only if the partner record is gone.

The partner's name. Null only if the partner record is gone.

heldForClawback.description: Partners not paid this run because their outstanding refund clawbacks are at least what they are owed (`amount`, before clawbacks). Their commissions stay approved and are paid, net, once enough accrues.

partnerName.description: The partner's name. Null only if the partner record is gone.

reason.description: Why the partner is on hold: `country_not_supported` (their declared country isn't served), `screening_review` (a possible sanctions-list match waits for OpenPartner's review), `screening_confirmed` (a confirmed match), or `screening_pending` (not screened yet; usually clears within the hour).

heldForCompliance.description: OpenPartner Cloud: Stripe payouts not made this run because the partner is on a compliance hold (`GET /payouts/holds`). Their commissions stay approved and are paid on the first run after the hold lifts. `amount` is what they are owed.

partnerName.description: The partner's name. Null only if the partner record is gone.

clawbackAmount.description: Refund clawbacks netted off this payout. `amount` is already net of them.

complianceWarning.description: A `manual` payout to a partner on a compliance hold. You send this money yourself, so the payout was still made: check before you send it.

partnerName.description: The partner's name. Null only if the partner record is gone.

sent.description: Set while (or once) a PayPal batch sends this payout in another currency; gone if PayPal returns it.

allOf.description: What PayPal was asked to send.

post.description:
Creates a partner and grants it programs.

- `sendInvite: false` creates the partner **active immediately** and sends no email. Use this when your own app is the partner's UI (headless / in-app referral). The default sends a magic-link invite.
- `portalAccess: false` keeps the partner out of the hosted partner portal: `POST /auth/signin` sends them nothing (it answers as it does for an unknown email), and no invite or portal email goes to them. It needs `sendInvite: false` (`400 invite_requires_portal_access` otherwise). Omitted, it is `true` for an invited partner and the tenant default (`GET /config/partner-access`) for one created without an invite. Change it later with `PATCH /partners/{id}`.
- `programIds` omitted grants **every current program**. Pass an explicit list (even `[]`) to control access.
- A coupon is auto-minted per granted program.
- Fires `partner.created`, then, for a `sendInvite: false` partner (active now), `partner.activated` with `invited: false`. An invited partner fires `partner.activated` when they accept.

**`partners:create`** is the scope for an in-app integration's runtime key: it can only create partners, and only without an invite or commission terms. A request with `sendInvite` omitted or `true`, a `commissionSnapshot` or `programCommissions` answers `403 forbidden_scope` with `required: "partners:write"`.

**`country`** (optional, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) is where the partner is based. OpenPartner Cloud doesn't serve some countries: a blocked one answers `422 country_not_supported`, and `"UA"` needs `outsideOccupiedRegions: true` (`422 occupied_region_confirmation_required` otherwise). An accepted country is recorded, and if it is blocked later, the partner's Stripe payouts are held. Self-hosted installs ignore it.

**OpenPartner Network:** this call shares nothing with the OpenPartner Network. A partner's name and email reach it only if the partner opts in themselves, while the tenant offers the Network (`autoEnroll` on, `GET /config/network`): they're asked on the join page, once on first portal sign-in, and in a portal setting. `metadata` is never sent. To keep customer-referral partners from being asked, turn offering off: `POST /config/network {"autoEnroll": false}`.

On OpenPartner Cloud the brand needs an active plan (`402 plan_required`) and an approved account (`403 brand_pending_review`).

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `partners:write` or `partners:create`.

patch.description:
`portalAccess: false` ends the partner's portal sessions and unused sign-in links at once. From then on `POST /auth/signin` sends them nothing, and no invite or portal email goes to them. Their partner API keys (`POST /partners/{id}/api-keys`) keep working; revoke those with `DELETE /api-keys/{keyId}`.

`portalAccess: true` sends nothing. An active partner can then request a sign-in link on the portal; one who never accepted an invite needs `POST /partners/{id}/invite`.

Fields this operation doesn't accept answer `400 invalid_body`.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `partners:write`.

post.description:
Creates many partners in one request: the way to load an existing customer base without spending your rate limit on one `POST /partners` per row.

Send `text/csv` with a header row: `email` and `name` (required), `activatedAt` (ISO-8601, default now) and `metadata` (a JSON object string, e.g. `"{""appUserId"":""u_1""}"`). Quoted fields may contain commas but not line breaks. Tools that can't send `text/csv` can POST `{"csv": "..."}` as JSON instead.

Unlike `POST /partners`, an import:
- grants every partner **every current program** (there is no `programIds`),
- sends no email, mints no coupons, fires no `partner.created` or `partner.activated` webhooks,
- gives every partner the tenant's default portal access for partners added without an invite (`GET /config/partner-access`),
- shares nothing with the OpenPartner Network: as with `POST /partners`, only a partner's own opt-in does.

Rows whose email already exists are reported as `skipped_email_taken` with the existing `partnerId`, so re-running an import is safe. `?dryRun=true` validates and reports without writing. The file is written in one transaction, so a failed import writes nothing. A repeated email later in the same file is skipped like one already on the roster. Send very large rosters in batches of a few thousand rows.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `partners:write`.

post.summary: Sign a partner in to the portal from your app
post.description:
Mints a link that signs the partner in to the partner portal, so your users go from your app to their referral dashboard without a second login. Call it from your backend when the user clicks through (a "Refer & earn" button that hits your server), and redirect the browser to `url` at once: it works **once**, for **five minutes**, and signs in whoever opens it. Don't email it, log it, or render it into a page ahead of time.

The link goes to your white-label domain when one is verified (`refer.example.com/auth/magic?…`), otherwise to the portal on OpenPartner's own domain. `returnTo` (a portal path such as `/links`) picks the page it lands on.

The partner must be one `POST /auth/signin` would email: active, not revoked, with portal access. Otherwise `409`: `partner_revoked`, `pending_review` (an applicant not yet approved), `portal_access_disabled` (turn it on with `PATCH /partners/{id}`), or `partner_not_activated` (invited, but hasn't accepted; partners created with `sendInvite: false` are active at once). The checks run again when the link is opened, along with the served-country check on the partner's own connection.

**`partners:signin`** is the scope for this, and nothing else grants it, `partners:write` included. The OpenPartner Network's federation key is refused even if it holds the scope. Portal sessions get `403 api_key_required`: this is a server-to-server call. Each key may mint 600 links a minute, and each partner 10 (`429 rate_limited`), and every link minted is recorded with the key that asked for it.

On OpenPartner Cloud the brand needs an approved account (`403 brand_pending_review`).

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `partners:signin`.

post.summary: Stitch a click to a user
post.description:
Links the click id (`cref`) a visitor arrived with to your user id. The browser SDK calls this on signup and login; your backend can call it instead if it receives the `cref`.

Repeat calls for the same pair are no-ops. Events already recorded for the user that have not attributed yet are attributed when the stitch lands (`backfilledAttributions`); an event that already attributed keeps its credit, and refunds and other corrective events are never attributed. Calling it on login too stitches a user who clicked on another device.

Unauthenticated by design. It accepts any origin (CORS) and is limited to 120 requests per minute per client IP. Use the same `userId` you later send to `POST /attribution/events`.

**Access:** public, no API key. Rate-limited per client IP.

Server-to-server conversion ingest. The event is attributed to the partner whose click the user was stitched to (within the program's window and model) and commissions accrue.

**Renewals.** Send each renewal as its own event with the same `userId` and `type` (one `invoice_paid` per payment). Once the customer has an attributed event of that type, each later one keeps that event's partners and weights, however old the click, while the program has `renewalsStayWithPartner` on (the default).

**Event types.** Any string is accepted. Two have built-in meaning:
- `signup` is the funnel's *signups* stage, as are `trial_started`, `subscription_created` and `invoice_paid` (`signup` and `trial_started` are *leads* in the timeseries).
- `invoice_paid` is the funnel's *paid* stage, and on OpenPartner Cloud it is billable GMV, as is `subscription_created`. Report payments as `invoice_paid`. Other types with a value still accrue commission but are not counted as GMV.

`value` is a JSON number in major units (`49.99`), not a string. Omit it for an event with no value; `null` is refused. `currency` is an ISO 4217 code in any case, stored upper case (`inr` is `INR`). Without one the event is stored in the brand's default currency (Settings → Program; USD unless changed), so send it whenever the brand takes more than one currency.

**Idempotency.** Always send `externalEventId`: your system's stable id for this one event (invoice id, order id, deal id + stage). A retry with the same key returns `200` with `replayed: true` and the original result, writing nothing. Reusing a key for a different userId, type, value or currency returns `409 external_event_id_conflict`. Keys are per tenant, up to 120 characters, and shared with `POST /coupons/redeem`.

**Refunds.** Report them to `POST /attribution/refunds`. A `refund` or `chargeback` event sent here is recorded but never attributed (`attribution.status` `corrective`) and reverses nothing.

**Don't report a payment twice.** If your Stripe account also sends webhooks to this deployment (`/webhooks/stripe`, single-tenant self-host), those payments are already recorded: invoices keyed by the Stripe event id, one-time Checkout payments by the Checkout Session id. Reporting the same payment here under your own invoice id records it a second time. Checkout Session ids are reserved for the webhook there: one (`cs_live_…`, `cs_test_…`) as the key returns `409 recorded_from_stripe`.

**Stripe connected (OpenPartner Cloud).** Once your Stripe account is connected through the OpenPartner Stripe App, Stripe invoices and Checkout payments are recorded from Stripe itself, keyed by the invoice or Checkout Session id. An `externalEventId` that is one of those ids (`in_…`, `cs_live_…`, `cs_test_…`) returns `409 recorded_from_stripe`: Stripe's record of the payment wins.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `events:write`.

post.summary: Record a conversion against a click
post.description:
For senders that hold a click id but never saw an identify: a lender reporting a funded loan, a CRM, an affiliate network. The click id reaches them through the destination URL's `{click_id}` macro, or the `cref` the router appends. One call stitches the click to a user and records the event, in one transaction.

Send `userId` when you have your own id for the user: attribution then follows the program's model across every click that user is stitched to, as on `POST /attribution/events`. Without it the click's own synthetic user is used, and this click alone is credited. Events recorded for the user before this stitch are not backfilled; `POST /attribution/identify` does that.

`value` and `currency` work as on `POST /attribution/events`: without a currency the event is stored in the brand's default currency.

**Scope.** Conversions are scoped to the tenant, not to a program. The click id already says which program the click came through, so there's no `programId` to send, and a click from any program in this tenant is accepted. A click id this tenant doesn't have is `404 click_not_found`. Keys with `events:write` (and the postback token) work across every program in the tenant, so a sender holding one can report against any of its clicks.

**Idempotency.** `externalEventId` is required. A retry with the same key returns `200` with `replayed: true` and the original result, even if the click has been flagged since. Keys are unique across the **whole tenant**: one namespace shared by `POST /attribution/events`, `GET /postback` (`txn_id`), `POST /coupons/redeem` and the Stripe webhook. Reusing a key for a different click, userId, type, value or currency returns `409 external_event_id_conflict`, and that conversion is not recorded. With your Stripe account connected, a Stripe invoice or Checkout Session id as the key returns `409 recorded_from_stripe`, as on `POST /attribution/events`, and so does a Checkout Session id on a single-tenant self-host whose Stripe webhook points at `/webhooks/stripe`. So:
- **One key per stage.** A loan reported as `approved` and later `loan_funded` needs two keys, e.g. `loan-881:approved` and `loan-881:funded`.
- **Prefix keys per sender.** Two suppliers' order ids can collide: `acme:loan-881:funded`, `zenlend:loan-881:funded`.

**Outcome.** Every `200` carries `outcome` (and sometimes `reason`), which says what the conversion came to: `attributed`, `no_matching_rule` (credited, but no commission rule takes this `type`, which usually means a typo'd stage name) or `not_attributed` (e.g. `outside_window`). The conversion is recorded in every case, so don't retry on these. Fix the cause and send the next conversion.

A click flagged by velocity limits or a revoked partner earns nothing: `422 click_flagged`.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `events:write`.

get.summary: Record a conversion from a postback URL
get.description:
`POST /attribution/conversions` for senders that can only fire a URL: affiliate networks, many lenders, tracking pixels. Same result: the click is stitched to a user and the event recorded, in one transaction.

```
GET /postback?click_id={click_id}&type=sale&amount=49.00&currency=USD&txn_id={transaction_id}&token=opcp_…
```

**The token is in the URL.** Proxies, browser history and the sender's own logs keep query strings, so treat a postback URL as leaked from the day you hand it out, and use `POST /attribution/conversions` with a Bearer key whenever the sender can set a header. The postback token is built for this: it records conversions and nothing else, is never accepted as a Bearer key (and an API key is never accepted as `token`), can be pinned to the sender's IPs (`ipAllowlist`), and rotating it on the Integrations page stops the old URL at once. OpenPartner's own request log redacts it. Always use `https://`.

**One token per tenant.** The token records conversions for every program in the tenant, so any sender holding it can report against any click. When several suppliers or networks send postbacks, pin the token to their addresses with `ipAllowlist` (`PATCH /conversion-postback`), and rotate it when one leaves.

**Idempotency.** `txn_id` is the `externalEventId`: a network re-firing the postback records once. Keys are unique across the whole tenant, in one namespace with `POST /attribution/conversions`, `POST /attribution/events`, `POST /coupons/redeem` and the Stripe webhook. Reusing one for a different conversion is `409 external_event_id_conflict`, and that conversion is not recorded. Send a different `txn_id` for each stage (`loan-881:approved`, `loan-881:funded`), prefixed per sender.

**Responses are plain text**, not JSON. A `200` is `ok` followed by what the conversion came to:

| Body | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ok attributed` | A partner was credited and earned commission. |
| `ok attributed no_commission` | Credited, but nothing accrued: the program has ended, a `first` rule already paid, a cap was reached, the amount was zero, or it's a renewal past the attribution window, which only `recurring` rules pay. |
| `ok no_matching_rule` | Credited, but no commission rule takes this `type`. Usually a typo'd stage name. Admin → Integrations lists these types. |
| `ok not_attributed outside_window` | No partner credited: the click is older than the program's attribution window. |
| `ok not_attributed no_click` | No partner credited: the partner was revoked. |
| `ok not_attributed` | A replay of a conversion that wasn't attributed the first time. |

All of these are `200` because the conversion is recorded: a retry would only replay it. Match on the `ok` prefix to tell success from an error. Errors are the bare code (`invalid_parameters` is followed by the offending names, e.g. `invalid_parameters: click_id, txn_id`). Every response is `Cache-Control: no-store`. `HEAD` answers `405` and records nothing, so a link checker can't create a conversion.

The token is checked before anything else, so a caller without one learns nothing about the parameters or clicks. Mint it under **Admin → Integrations** (or `POST /conversion-postback/token`).

**Access:** the conversion postback token in the `token` query parameter. API keys are not accepted, as a Bearer header or as `token`.

post.description:
Reports that a conversion was refunded, in full or in part, or charged back. Reference the conversion by the `externalEventId` you sent with it (`conversionExternalEventId`, preferred) or by the `eventId` OpenPartner returned (`conversionEventId`): exactly one. Conversions recorded from Stripe, by the self-host Stripe webhook or, on OpenPartner Cloud, the OpenPartner Stripe App, can be referenced too, but their Stripe refunds are already handled there; don't report those twice.

The refund is recorded as a corrective event (type `refund` or `chargeback`, a negative `value`) that is never attributed, and the conversion's commissions follow it. Each commission ends up worth its original amount times the share of the conversion the customer kept:
- **Not yet paid** (`accrued`, `approved`): reversed, firing `commission.reversed` (reason `refund` or `chargeback`) and the partner's postback. On a partial refund a replacement commission for the kept amount follows (`commission.accrued` with `replacesCommissionId`), keeping the original's status and accrual date, so its holdback doesn't restart.
- **Already paid**: it stays paid. A negative adjustment records the refunded revenue the partner holds (`clawback_recorded`). OpenPartner deducts it from the partner's next manual or self-hosted Stripe Connect payout; a partner who owes more than they are due is not paid until enough accrues. Funded Stripe Connect payouts on hosted OpenPartner don't deduct it: recover those with the partner.
- **In a payout right now**: left alone (`held_in_transfer`). Retry the same request once the payout settles.

`amount` is in major units and defaults to everything not yet refunded. Partial refunds add up: two refunds of 30 and 20 on a 100 conversion leave each commission at 50%. A conversion with no `value` can only be refunded in full. A `chargeback` reverses commissions like a refund, so report it once it is final, not when a dispute opens.

**Idempotency.** `externalEventId` is required: your id for this refund (refund id, credit note id). A retry with the same key returns `200` with `replayed: true`, records nothing new, and re-applies the refund, which also finishes any commission that was held in transfer. Reusing a key for a different conversion, kind or amount returns `409 external_event_id_conflict`. Keys share one namespace with `POST /attribution/events`.

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `events:write`.

post.summary: Reverse an accrued or approved commission
post.description:
Fires `commission.reversed` with `reason: "manual"`.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

A reward that isn't tied to a sale: a launch bonus, a contest prize, a thank-you. It is written as a bonus and one commission (`source: "bonus"` in commission lists, `bonusId` set, no `attributionId`), so it is approved, paid and reversed like any commission, but it never counts as a sale, a lead or toward a tier.

- `amount` is in major units with at most two decimals (`400 invalid_amount` otherwise).
- Approved at once and paid in the next payout run. `hold: true` holds it for the program's holdback first (`programId`), or the partner's own.
- `externalRef` makes a retry safe: the same value returns the original (`200`, `replayed: true`). The same `externalRef` with a different partner, program, amount or currency is `409 external_ref_conflict`.
- Fires `bonus.awarded`, then `bonus.approved` unless held. Never `commission.*`.
- On OpenPartner Cloud's commission-floor fee terms a bonus is billed at the commission rate, like a fixed commission with no sale amount.

Called with the brand's OpenPartner Network federation key, the bonus is recorded as `source: "network"`; every other caller pays `manual` bonuses. On OpenPartner Cloud the brand needs an active plan (`402 plan_required`) and an approved account (`403 brand_pending_review`).

**Access:** admin key, or a scoped key with `bonuses:write`.

post.description:
Sends the next PayPal Payouts batch of a run, in one currency, with your active PayPal app: the same payouts a PayPal file would take (partners whose payout details are a PayPal email, a currency PayPal sends, under PayPal's per-payment limit, nothing on a do-not-pay hold), up to 5,000. The money goes from your PayPal balance to the partners; it never passes through OpenPartner.

The payouts are stamped with the batch id (`exportId`, `via: "api"`) before anything is sent, so they are in no other file or batch. The batch id is also PayPal's `sender_batch_id` and `PayPal-Request-Id`: a re-send after a timeout or crash reaches the same batch, and PayPal never pays one twice.

PayPal pays asynchronously. Follow the batch with `GET /payouts/paypal-batches/{batchId}`: paid items confirm their payouts; failed, returned or refunded ones go back to pending (and your admins are emailed); unclaimed ones wait for the partner to claim them.

**INR.** PayPal can't send INR (it isn't a PayPal API currency): an INR payout is `currency_not_supported` unless you turn on `POST /config/paypal-payouts` `{"sendUnsupportedAs": "USD"}`. Then quote first (`POST /payouts/runs/{runId}/paypal-batches/quote`) and send with `{"currency": "INR", "sendAs": "USD", "quoteId": "…"}` within 15 minutes: the batch sends exactly the quoted payouts at exactly the quoted ECB rate. A quote that expired is `409 quote_expired`; one whose payouts changed since (another batch took one, a partner changed their PayPal email, PayPal gave one back) or whose PayPal app is no longer the active one is `409 quote_changed`; quote again. The payouts stay in INR; each one's stamp records what was sent (`conversion`).

With your **sandbox** app active, the batch is a rehearsal: PayPal's sandbox moves test money, so no payout is marked paid, and once PayPal settles every item the payouts go back to pending (`rehearsal` on the batch says what happened).

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.

Quotes the next batch the send would make: the European Central Bank reference rate (crossed through EUR, published once a business day), its date, each payout's USD amount (its INR amount × rate, rounded half up to the cent on its own), the INR and USD totals, and a signed `quoteId` valid for 15 minutes.

Send with `POST /payouts/runs/{runId}/paypal-batches` `{"currency": "INR", "sendAs": "USD", "quoteId": "…"}`. Nothing is held: the send checks the payouts are still exactly these. A payout over PayPal's per-payment limit in USD, or under a cent, is listed in `leftOut` instead; when that's every payout, the `404 nothing_to_send` carries the `leftOut` list.

The rate is the ECB mid-market reference rate; you send that USD amount from your PayPal balance. PayPal then converts it to INR for the partner's Indian bank at PayPal's own rate, which is between the partner and PayPal. If the ECB rates can't be read, nothing is quoted (`503 fx_unavailable`): no rate is ever guessed.

That is your decision as the data's controller, so it is off by default. Omitted fields keep their value. Also on Admin → Settings.

**Access:** admin key only. Scoped keys get `403 forbidden`.
